english: Let $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}$ be two non-collinear vectors, and let $P$, $Q$ and $S$ be the points with position vectors $3\overrightarrow{a}-\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}$ and $-\overrightarrow{a}+2\overrightarrow{b}$, respectively, with respect to the origin $O$. The line through $S$ parallel to the vector $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}$ meets the line $PQ$ at the point $R$. If $\overrightarrow{OR}=\lambda\overrightarrow{a}+\mu\overrightarrow{b}$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are real numbers, then the value of $\lambda\mu$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\overrightarrow{a}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{b}$ दो असरेख सदिश हैं, तथा मूलबिन्दु $O$ के सापेक्ष $P$, $Q$ और $S$ वे बिन्दु हैं जिनके स्थिति सदिश क्रमशः $3\overrightarrow{a}-\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}$ तथा $-\overrightarrow{a}+2\overrightarrow{b}$ हैं। $S$ से होकर सदिश $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}$ के समान्तर रेखा, रेखा $PQ$ से बिन्दु $R$ पर मिलती है। यदि $\overrightarrow{OR}=\lambda\overrightarrow{a}+\mu\overrightarrow{b}$ है, जहाँ $\lambda$ तथा $\mu$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं, तो $\lambda\mu$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: $\overrightarrow{PQ}=(\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b})-(3\overrightarrow{a}-\overrightarrow{b})=-2\overrightarrow{a}+2\overrightarrow{b}$, which is not parallel to $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}$, so the two lines meet in exactly one point.

A point of the line through $S$ parallel to $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}$: $(-\overrightarrow{a}+2\overrightarrow{b})+t(\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b})=(t-1)\overrightarrow{a}+(t+2)\overrightarrow{b}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$.

At $R$ the two expressions are equal. Since $\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{b}$ are non-collinear, $x\overrightarrow{a}+y\overrightarrow{b}=\overrightarrow{0}$ only for $x=y=0$, so the coefficients of $\overrightarrow{a}$ and of $\overrightarrow{b}$ must be equal separately:
Adding the two equations: $2=2t+1$, so $t=\dfrac12$; then $2s=t+3=\dfrac72$, $s=\dfrac74$.
By uniqueness of the coefficients, $\lambda=-\dfrac12$ and $\mu=\dfrac52$, so $\lambda\mu=-\dfrac54=-1.25$.
originality_note: New: two lines given only through position vectors in the basis a, b (one through two points, one through a point with a given direction); the intersection is found purely by comparing coefficients in the plane (way 5). Closest known: intersection of two cevians of a triangle in vector form. Different because: no triangle is involved, the lines are arbitrary and the answer is a product of both coordinates of R.
blueprint_concepts: Linear combination theorem in a plane

concept_use.Linear combination theorem in a plane: Since a and b are non-collinear, (3-2s)a+(2s-1)b = (t-1)a+(t+2)b forces equal coefficients, giving t = 1/2, and then lambda, mu are unique.

Checked that PQ is not parallel to a+b, so R exists and is unique; stated that lambda, mu are real. Changed: No change.

justification: Routine chain: two parametric forms, the linear-combination theorem, a 2x2 linear system. No insight required; same level as the routine vector chain of 2026-P2-Q1 (L2), a step above the direct checks of 2023-P2-Q4 (L1) because of the numerical format.
